items.title: Hermes Lab
items.tagline: A measured integration laboratory for meaningful improvements, not a monolithic fork.
items.problem: Uncoordinated integrations produce attractive demos whose causal value, provenance and promotion boundary are unclear. A consistent downstream experiment program makes alternatives comparable.
items.outcome: Compare bounded intelligence, structured observation, harness mechanisms and cognitive-state virtualization on matched Hermes tasks before choosing independently promotable slices.
journeys: A contributor chooses a hypothesis with a fixed baseline, candidate, task set and budget.
An operator compares the same workflow across baseline and one changed mechanism, seeing verified success, latency and cost separately.
A maintainer receives one small upstream-ready change with RED→GREEN evidence rather than a merged experimental stack.
ownership: Hermes remains the execution host and approval authority.
z0intelligence owns decision/state research; SoL-Pi owns observation projections; RLM owns state compilation; z0evals owns frozen comparison results.
Each experiment runs in its own branch and exports sanitized receipts; no parallel runtimes become authoritative.
phases: Reconcile the RFC-0 tracks and S1–S5 matrix; register baseline and candidate revisions.
Run shadow/frozen comparisons separately before any active single-factor test.
Select independently useful outcomes for narrow upstream review; retain failed experiments as falsification evidence.
acceptance: Every experiment has an exact identity join, version pin and independently verified outcome or explicit unknown.
For any active path, failure injection proves safe fallback and no duplicated physical action.
Report paired success, token and p50/p95 latency deltas rather than a single aggregate score.
No result is described as merged upstream without a linked upstream merge.
risks: Research scope creep into production behavior without a gate.
Metrics that report token reductions while hiding failures or setup cost.
metrics: Verified outcome per fixed task family
Latency and tokens per turn with cold/warm splits
Number of independently promotable small fixes
items.credit: Research and integration derive from Hermes contributors, z0intelligence, SoL-Pi, OMP/RLM and their original maintainers. Each slice retains its own donor history.

items.title: NanoJev & Bounded Intelligence
items.tagline: Spend frontier-model cognition only where the decision genuinely needs it.
items.problem: Routine reversible choices can consume the same expensive reasoning resources as difficult work. Replacing them blindly risks illegality, degraded decisions and opaque failures.
items.outcome: Use small, typed decision specialists for known finite-choice tasks while retaining Hermes legality gates and independent outcome verification.
journeys: Hermes exposes a finite legal candidate set for a model/tool decision.
A local backend returns a distribution, confidence, latency and its version; the baseline still executes in shadow mode.
After enough paired outcomes, an operator enables one bounded lane with instant fallback to the known-safe path.
ownership: Hermes owns legal actions, models, permissions and actual execution.
z0intelligence/DecisionBackend owns candidate scoring and receipts; Jev can be a reference observer, not ground truth.
Routing never approves a privileged action or changes security policy.
phases: Survey reversible decision seams and baseline legality.
Collect at least 20 real paired shadow decisions across the specified backend matrix.
Evaluate equal-or-better verified outcome before selectively enabling one cheap fast path.
acceptance: Preserve complete candidate set, supported probabilities, selected baseline decision and trace identity.
Backend outage or invalid suggestion leaves Hermes behavior unchanged.
Compare cold/warm latency, frontier tokens, dollar cost and outcome; report disagreement instead of hiding it.
No active promotion on agreement rate alone.
risks: Learned judge used as an approval authority.
Unmeasured local-model residency or warmup erasing nominal savings.
metrics: Avoided frontier tokens at non-decreased task success
Shadow disagreement rate by decision family
Warm/cold decision latency and model footprint
items.credit: Jev and community Hermes Jev plugins remain independent donor projects; preserve plugin author attribution and typed-check semantics.

items.title: SoL-Pi ObservationPack
items.tagline: Structured, identity-preserving perception for reliable computer use.
items.problem: Raw screenshots and long accessibility dumps can obscure element identity, repeat redundant context and make actions stale before execution.
items.outcome: Compare structured ObservationPack projections with the original computer-use observations without changing the controlling executor until evidence supports it.
journeys: A desktop observation is captured and retained in original form.
A pure projection emits structured elements, provenance, identity and elapsed projection time.
On the same frozen task, observers compare action agreement, stale-target rejection and verified postconditions.
ownership: Hermes controls the computer-use action loop and approvals.
SoL-Pi owns the ObservationPack projection and shared configuration contract.
The baseline observation stays available; a projection failure must not silently change an authorized target.
phases: Survey observation sources and pin the existing plugin contract.
Run frozen desktop, modal, scroll, near-duplicate and partial-tree fixtures.
Only after decision-equivalence tests, allow a bounded active path behind capability gates.
acceptance: Retain reference element IDs and before/after provenance across projection.
A stale view after an action cannot be reused to justify a mutation.
Report steps, outcome, context bytes and projection overhead on paired tasks.
No simultaneous Action Fusion/ObservationPack changes in the first experiment.
risks: Misidentifying visually similar elements.
Mistaking a shorter observation for better task performance.
items.credit: SoL-Pi's source authors and NVIDIA contributors retain provenance; downstream projections are not represented as native Hermes ownership.

items.title: Hermes × OMP Harness
items.tagline: Transfer proven harness mechanisms, not entire application architectures.
items.problem: Two capable agent harnesses have independently evolved useful edit, batching and rendering semantics. Porting wholesale code risks drift and conflicting runtime ownership.
items.outcome: Evaluate small, measurable cross-harness improvements such as hash-anchored edits, safe tool loops and isolated workers.
journeys: An engineer identifies one OMP behavior and an existing Hermes analog.
The candidate is implemented in an isolated lane with equivalence and negative tests.
A reviewer sees matched speed/quality numbers and a minimal source-documented patch.
ownership: Hermes owns its state, tools and permission checks.
OMP is a reference for UX/harness invariants, not a second execution engine.
All borrowed code must retain original license, authors and test semantics.
phases: Build a scorecard of portable invariants; reject duplicate capabilities.
Select one small port with a deterministic behavioral baseline.
Run paired task success, latency and token measurements; propose a narrow PR only for a positive result.
acceptance: Evidence identifies the exact borrowed behavior and human source authors.
Prove ordered side effects are not deduplicated or reordered incorrectly.
Tests include failure/retry behavior and avoid introducing shadow stores.
A change with no measurable benefit stays downstream or is dropped.
risks: Accidental copying of context or permission internals.
Code duplication without upstream acceptance.
metrics: Code size and operational complexity added

sources.label: OMP by Can Bölük and contributors

items.credit: Credit Can Bölük and OMP contributors for source patterns; preserve NousResearch author provenance for Hermes-side work.

items.title: RLM · Cognitive State
items.tagline: Keep the transcript as audit truth while compiling the cognition that actually matters.
items.problem: Replaying an ever-growing transcript burdens models, caches and budgets. Deleting old messages merely because they are old can destroy causal evidence.
items.outcome: Compile evidence-backed State Packets for each information need while preserving a canonical audit transcript and exact source revisions.
journeys: Hermes stores the full transcript for resume, review and recovery.
A shadow compiler builds the intended model-visible state from evidence, contradictions and unresolved gaps.
After falsification, one bounded active mode replaces only selected context, with native-context fallback.
ownership: Hermes retains transcript/session authority and approval lifecycle.
RLM handles state compilation; z0intelligence owns State Packet identity and evidence linking.
z0evals hosts frozen recall/exact-identifier cohorts and independent verification.
phases: Emit shadow packets but send normal context; quantify source access, size and compile time.
Test packet injection with contradiction, supersession, cache invalidation and replay guards.
Run paired active/context-baseline trials only after safe fallback and no-omission gates.
acceptance: Never destroy or mutate the audit transcript as a side effect of compression.
Exact identifiers and source revisions survive in evidence refs; missing sources force an explicit gap.
A source revision invalidates stale packets; duplicate replay never double-injects.
Report root-input and total tokens alongside independently verified success.
risks: Compaction gives fluent but unsupported conclusions.
Double injections or cache prefix disruption increase real cost.
items.credit: OMP/RLM and z0intelligence maintainers own their donor mechanisms; preserve evidence and comparison provenance.

items.title: Outcome-Verified Evaluation
items.tagline: One reproducible receipt from hypothesis to independently verified outcome.
items.problem: A passing unit suite or a low token bill says little about whether an agent completed a task safely. Cross-project experiments need stable joins and failure-injection receipts.
items.outcome: Build a common evaluation envelope across Hermes, z0int, RLM and SoL-Pi, then use factorial controls to attribute improvement.
journeys: An experiment launches with frozen fixture and exact project/model revisions.
The evaluator joins trace/session/turn IDs to measured actions and the independent verifier result.
A maintainer sees baseline vs candidate, uncertainty, failure cases, unknowns and source-specific follow-up.
ownership: z0evals owns evaluation cohorts and frozen external result bundles.
Hermes executes experiments but the verifying agent must be independent of the candidate where feasible.
A thin envelope normalizes only fields without an existing authoritative owner.
phases: Define failure-mode receipts: backend outage, stale observation, missing evidence, OOM, duplicate replay.
Run baseline, single-factor Z/R/S arms and only then combinations.
Publish sanitized paired results; retain private trace inputs locally.
acceptance: Unknown verification remains unknown, never counted as success.
Replays cannot mint duplicate external side effects.
Every report names exact code/config/test revisions and a matching baseline.
No global-stack winner from unmatched aggregates.
risks: Verifier leakage into the system being evaluated.
Composed mechanisms obscuring attribution.
items.credit: Hermes Lab measurement work cites original owner repos and upstream issue reporters in every exported receipt.

items.title: Unified Memory & Recall
items.tagline: Durable, grounded recall across sessions without replacing the source of truth.
items.problem: Transient chat context loses project state, exact identifiers and contradictory evidence, while uncontrolled recall can disclose unrelated material or resurrect stale claims.
items.outcome: A permission-aware recall layer that retrieves versioned evidence and supports compaction without silently overriding Hermes's existing memory provider.
journeys: A resumed session can retrieve an exact decision and the source it came from.
An agent writes a proposed memory after a confirmed outcome, with expiry, scope and provenance.
A user can audit or invalidate a stale fact; recall must distinguish current evidence from history.
ownership: Hermes remains the owner of session/memory authorization and persistence.
The unified store/prototype is a downstream research carrier; external memory prefetch metrics are opt-in.
Memory retrieval must respect source scope and the existing provider configuration.
phases: Reconcile the existing `study/hermes-unified-memory-56` prototype against current Hermes memory interfaces.
Add deterministic exact-recall, stale-source, consent and contradiction tests.
Benchmark observed recall quality, retrieval latency and cache effect before a narrow integration.
acceptance: No cross-session/profile information leak or secret in logs/metrics.
An older summary cannot win over a newer verified source without explicit conflict.
Measure recall on exact IDs and provenance, not just semantic similarity.
Provider init failures do not silently disable the configured memory backend.
risks: Single giant memory store with unverifiable provenance.
Over-prefetching harming latency and privacy.
metrics: Exact identifier recall at source revision
items.credit: Hermes memory-provider contributors and independent storage/search projects retain original provenance; no source data is embedded into the public spec.

items.title: Semantic Computer Use
items.tagline: Observe once, choose safely, execute bounded actions, verify what changed.
items.problem: GUI automation that guesses from pixels alone can be slow, brittle and unsafe when UI state changes between observation and action.
items.outcome: A semantic/visual control plane for Hermes computer use with typed targets, state revisions, safe batching and postcondition checks.
journeys: The agent observes a UI element using semantic hints with screenshot fallback.
It proposes a short ordered action sequence against the observed revision.
After execution, it verifies the intended result and stops/escalates on stale or uncertain effects.
ownership: Only Hermes's established computer-use tool driver executes actions and enforces approvals.
trycua/cua and structured observation donors supply optional semantic control and measurements.
Local decision scoring is advisory and must not authorize an action.
phases: Instrument observe→decide→act→verify timings on Linux with a frozen fixture cohort.
Add capability detection and stale-observation guards; retain order-sensitive keyboard actions.
Run real-desktop matched tasks before proposing any Windows/remote expansion.
acceptance: A stale/changed target forces reobservation before consequential action.
Order-significant duplicate keystrokes are never removed.
Unknown tool completion cannot be replayed blindly.
Compare verified task success and end-to-end latency, not just backend throughput.
risks: Replay of a partially applied GUI mutation.
A semantic target referring to the wrong window or host.
metrics: Actions and model calls per task
items.credit: trycua/cua and original GUI-driver authors remain credited; preserve Hermès executor ownership and consent boundaries.

items.title: Typed Workflow Orchestration
items.tagline: Reusable multi-step work with explicit authority, contracts and bounded delegation.
items.problem: Agent workflows become fragile when tools silently gain new authority, messages lose identity across steps or a second scheduler competes with Hermes recovery.
items.outcome: Represent multi-step intent as typed, auditable execution graphs while keeping Hermes as the only executor/approval owner.
journeys: An operator previews a workflow graph with parameters, expected effects and scope.
Hermes executes eligible steps with checkpoints, budgets and human approvals.
A failed/retried run resumes safely from receipts rather than repeating uncertain side effects.
ownership: AODL/HOTL validates graph contracts and legality; it is not a scheduler.
Hermes owns tools, sessions, secrets, approvals and recovery.
AgentRun/compatible plugins are optional workflow surfaces after duplicate-checking existing community engines.
phases: Compare AgentRun DSL against Hermes's current workflow capabilities and community plugins.
Expose a typed preview without executing and verify DAG schema, dependencies and side-effect classes.
Run one bounded workflow with deterministic replay, revision and authorization receipts.
acceptance: Cycles, invalid tool contracts and unauthorized side effects fail closed.
A partial failure can be resumed without duplicating irreversible actions.
No new plugin bypasses Hermes's permission or session ownership.
Execution receipts preserve source graph and exact revision.
risks: Duplicating durable scheduler state.
Promoting speculative plugin capabilities as core requirements.
items.credit: AgentRun (Parcha) authors, AODL authors, Hermes and existing community workflow-plugin maintainers retain credit.

items.title: Bend Proof Verification
items.tagline: A small plugin that turns formal verification into structured, reproducible evidence.
items.problem: An agent cannot safely equate a command's successful exit with proof that the intended source semantics were certified. Translations, imported dependencies and cache changes threaten reproducibility.
items.outcome: An opt-in `bend_verify` tool producing a fail-closed, source-bound and replayable proof verdict.
journeys: Hermes sends a bounded project/proof path to a standalone verifier tool.
The tool runs the installed Bend binary with shell invocation disabled and captures input/versions.
The response clearly separates supported verification, inconclusive results and source/translation mismatch.
ownership: Hermes orchestrates; Bend/BendTT is the verification authority.
Plugin owns path validation, local proof snapshots, offline settings and structured receipts.
No proof result bypasses a human approval or replaces independent source behavior tests.
phases: Maintain minimal proof adapter with path escape and bypass resistance.
Qualify each Bend release with source↔certified semantics oracle, including negative proof cases.
Add immutable import-closure identities and offline replay before accepting remote dependencies.
acceptance: Unsupported version, path escape, bad import and ambiguity fail closed.
Verified emitted book agrees with observed source semantics on every pinned oracle.
An offline replay returns the same verdict for identical captured dependencies.
Reported proofs preserve original researchers' bug and reproduction credit.
risks: Semantic drift despite green proof tool output.
Network imports resolved differently during replay.
items.credit: Bend maintainers and @Vacrin's original semantic-drift diagnosis and @quimmedes's independent kernel reproduction are essential provenance.
